headline: Geopolitics, Earnings Sway Market Sentiment
summary: A widening geopolitical conflict between the U.S. and Iran pushed crude oil prices higher amid disruption to key transit routes, weighing on market sentiment alongside earnings.
why: Crude oil is a core global energy commodity, and supply disruptions in Middle East transit routes feed directly into fuel costs, inflation expectations and equity valuations.
why_moved: Crude oil prices spiked further as the U.S.-Iran conflict disrupted key transit routes, overwhelming other market drivers.
